ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, this is a circular-ring power generation device: a conducting rod with resistance R=4 Ω is bent into a closed circular ring of radius L=0.2 m, the center of the circle is O, and COD is a diameter. A load resistor R1=1 Ω is connected between O and D. Throughout the whole circular ring there is a uniform magnetic field B=0.5 T passing perpendicularly through the plane of the ring. The conducting rod OA with resistance r=1 Ω moves uniformly against the circular ring, with angular velocity ω=300 rad/s. When OA reaches OC, what is the electric power of the circular ring?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, this is a circular-ring power generation device: a conducting rod with resistance R=4 Ω is bent into a closed circular ring of radius L=0.2 m, the center of the circle is O, and COD is a diameter. A load resistor R1=1 Ω is connected between O and D. Throughout the whole circular ring there is a uniform magnetic field B=0.5 T passing perpendicularly through the plane of the ring. The conducting rod OA with resistance r=1 Ω moves uniformly against the circular ring, with angular velocity ω=300 rad/s. When OA reaches OC, what is the electric power of the circular ring?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a circular ring (drawn as an elliptical perspective shape), the left end is labeled C, the right end is labeled D, the center of the circle is O, and C, O, D are on the same horizontal dashed-line diameter. From O to a point A on the circular ring there is a rotatable conducting rod, labeled with resistance r. Between O and D, a load resistor R1 is connected through an external wire, and R1 is drawn in the branch above the circular ring. Then reason: When the conducting rod OA reaches OC, the sliding rod is equivalent to a motional electromotive source. The motional electromotive force is ε = (1/2)BωL^2 = (1/2)×0.5×300×(0.2)^2 = 3 V, and the conducting rod's own resistance serves as the internal resistance r = 1 Ω. The total resistance of the fixed circular ring is R = 4 Ω; the upper and lower two semicircular resistances from C to D are equal, each being R/2 = 2 Ω; these two semicircles are in parallel between the two ends C and D, and the equivalent resistance is 2 Ω // 2 Ω = 1 Ω. This parallel circular-ring part is in series with the load resistor R1 = 1 Ω between O-D, so the equivalent resistance of the external circuit is 1 Ω + 1 Ω = 2 Ω. The current of the whole circuit is I = ε/(r + 2 Ω) = 3/(1+2) = 1 A. The total current flowing through the C-D circular-ring parallel part is 1 A. Since the two semicircular resistances are the same, the current is distributed equally, and the current in each semicircle is 0.5 A. The power consumed by the circular ring itself is P_ring = 2×(0.5)^2×2 = 1 W.
